briefing.prose:
Findings: The alert fired on the dead-letter queue's depth, and the rows that took it over the threshold were all one shape: four bulk_api_sync jobs whose three attempts to reach partner-api.internal each timed out after 30s with nothing acknowledged downstream, so no partial write survived any of them. All four were classified replay_safe and all four were replayed in one call; the queue now holds three rows and none of them is in that category. The three that remain are not this incident and each needs something a retry cannot give: f030f975-974e-5ce3-aa6b-444136507d86 is a CSV upload carrying a non-numeric value in an integer column, classified human_required, which needs the uploader to fix the file; af67d1b1-13f8-5a2c-8c44-66ec5564597d was rate-limited by the partner with a 120s retry-after; and 97d91272-9774-5b8e-980b-f0d2fa6ed619 could not reach the SMTP relay at all.


Recommendation: Watch the depth for ten minutes to confirm the replayed jobs do not return; if any of them does, partner-api.internal is still failing and its owner needs paging rather than another replay. The two wait_and_replay rows are worth a deferred replay once their dependencies answer — the rate-limited one after its 120s window, the SMTP one once smtp.mailer.internal is reachable. f030f975-974e-5ce3-aa6b-444136507d86 needs a person: its payload is wrong, not its timing.
